newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's of London appoints disciplinary board.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's of London appoints disciplinary board.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Friday it has appointed a seven-strong disciplinary board.
The insurance market said Matthew Patient, a former member of the ruling council, was to be chairman of the new body.
Christopher Rome, director of Cox Insurance and former marine insurance underwriter, will be deputy chairman.

These appointments come ahead of an announcement expected shortly, which is to detail around a dozen appointments to a panel, whose brief will be to report within six months on how Lloyd's should be regulated.
The establishment of the disciplinary board was approved by the insurance market's ruling council in August, as part of a radical overhaul of its disciplinary regime.
It decided then to introduce a new three-tier system of proceedings designed to accelerate disciplinary action and to extend the definition of misconduct.
